title: decentralized-trace-proxy-dispatcher-with-deadline-propagation
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Summary: Build a decentralized Trace Proxy Dispatcher service that can route spans and trace envelopes to different backend endpoints (Tempo, Jaeger, third-party vendors) on a per-tenant and per-request basis while preserving deadline/timeout propagation, sampling hints, and span ordering. This component lives in front of our existing OTLP ingest layer and is intended to be lightweight, fault-tolerant, and backpressure-aware.

Goals:
- Route by tenant policy, route tags in trace attributes, and dynamic config from Console.
- Propagate request deadlines/timeouts into downstream exporter clients so that long queues or slow backends do not violate end-to-end SLOs.
- Maintain sampling flags and span ordering where possible; avoid reparenting or re-timestamping spans unless explicit normalization is required.
- Support both OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP ingress, plus transform to Jaeger/Thrift or Tempo envelope when required.
- Provide observability (per-tenant metrics, queue lengths, per-backend latency percentiles, and drop counters) and a safe rollout path (canary by tenant).

Design notes / trade-offs:
1) Deadline propagation model: honor incoming gRPC deadlines when present. For HTTP requests without deadline, derive a default from tenant policy. If a downstream exporter call cannot complete before the deadline, return a truncated success with a partial-ack metric and avoid retrying beyond the deadline. This prevents head-of-line blocking.

2) Ordering guarantees vs throughput: full strict ordering requires head-of-line locking per-trace which reduces throughput. We'll provide best-effort ordering scoped to per-tenant and per-ingest-shard, and documented cases where ordering may be relaxed under high load.

3) Schema transformation: implement transparent in-flight translations with a plug-in adapter interface. Default adapters: OTLP->OTLP passthrough, OTLP->Jaeger, OTLP->Tempo envelope. Adapters run in a dedicated worker pool to limit costly transformations affecting fast-path.

4) Backpressure and buffering: implement an elastic in-memory window per-backend with LRU eviction policy by tenant. On sustained pressure, use sampling hints (if available) to drop low-priority traces first and emit a per-tenant drop report to metrics and dead-letter storage (S3) for later inspection.

5) Authentication & credential rotation: the dispatcher will fetch per-backend credentials from Vault/KV and cache them with refresh windows. If credential retrieval fails for >2 minutes, mark backend as degraded and route to fallback (if configured).

Acceptance criteria:
- Can route a representative 10k RPS synthetic trace stream to Tempo and Jaeger concurrently without exceeding 99th percentile latency budget of 300ms for routing decision (not downstream ingest).
- Deadlines from gRPC requests are honored and visible in dispatcher traces. When downstream timeouts occur, dispatcher increments a metric and returns partial success to caller within the original deadline.
- End-to-end test: tenant can configure a canary rule to send 5% of traces to a secondary backend; we verify dual-write consistency for a randomized sample.
- Observability: dashboards for dispatcher queue length, per-backend 50/95/99 latencies, drop rates, and credential rotation failures are created and linked in the ticket.

Implementation tasks (high level):
- API layer: accept OTLP/gRPC and OTLP/HTTP; parse tenant hints and attach routing metadata.
- Routing engine: config-driven policy evaluator with in-memory cache and Console sync hook.
- Exporter clients: deadline-aware clients for gRPC/HTTP with graceful cancellation and limited retry windows.
- Adapters: plugin interface and three initial adapters (OTLP passthrough, Jaeger, Tempo).
- Metrics/logging: Prometheus metrics, structured logs (JSON) with trace_id/tenant_id, and Grafana dashboards.
- E2E tests: load test harness (k6 or custom) and golden-trace verification harness.

Risks & mitigations:
- Risk: transformation costs could create latencies and memory spikes. Mitigation: adapter worker pools with backpressure signaling, plus circuit-breaker to drop transformations during burst.
- Risk: dual-write inconsistency could go undetected. Mitigation: implement deterministic sampling probe that dual-writes identical sample traces and compares hashes; emit alerts when mismatch rate > 0.1%.
- Risk: credential outages blocking routing. Mitigation: fallback routes and degraded-mode policy (emit metric and write to dead-letter).

Artifacts and links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Trace+Proxy+Dispatcher+Design (draft)
- Schema adapters README: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/trace-adapters
- Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/trace-proxy/pull/142 (WIP branch)
comments: 2025-02-12 - Maya Chen: Created ticket and initial design draft posted to Confluence. Asked infra for capacity guidance for an initial canary cluster.

2025-02-13 - Ravi Patel: Spike completed to measure adapter transform latencies (OTLP->Jaeger). Median transform ~0.8ms, p99 ~18ms under 1k RPS on dev machine. Recorded in spike notes: https://drive.redwood.ai/notes/trace-proxy-spike.md

2025-02-15 - Design review (Alex Gomez): Requested clearer docs on ordering guarantees; suggested best-effort semantic and explicit note that strict ordering is not provided during overload. Added as acceptance criteria item.
2025-02-17 - Security (Priya Nair): Reviewed credential rotation plan; requested rotation audit events be emitted to audit-log service. Added to implementation tasks.

2025-02-19 - Ravi Patel: Initial PR created (WIP). Hooked up Console feature flag for per-tenant routing config. Load-run 2k RPS synthetic succeeded with acceptable routing latency; observed increased p99 when adapters enabled — next step is adapter worker pool tuning.
2025-02-20 - Maya Chen: PM review: prioritize dashboards and alerting (drop-rate > 0.5%) for rollout. Assigned `observability-platform` owner to create Grafana panels.
acceptance_criteria: Routing latency (decision time) p99 <= 300ms at target RPS with adapters disabled, <= 450ms with adapters enabled
Dispatcher honors gRPC deadlines and returns within original deadline in 99% of successful requests
Per-tenant canary dual-write validation test with mismatch rate < 0.1%
Dashboards coverage: queue length, per-backend latency p50/p95/p99, drop rates, credential rotation failures, and partial-ack counts
test_plan: Unit tests for routing policy evaluator and adapter interface
Integration tests: OTLP/gRPC ingress -> dispatcher -> Tempo/Jaeger in test cluster
Load test: incremental RPS up to 10k synthetic traces with realistic size distribution
Chaos test: simulate backend latency spikes and credential rotation failures to validate fallbacks and metrics
Dual-write consistency probe that samples 0.5% of traces and compares hashes in CI
rollout_plan: Feature-flagged in Console; start with internal tenants only
Canary: 1 node pool, 1% traffic for 24h -> 5% traffic for 48h -> 25% for 72h with automated metric checks
Alerting gates: if drop_rate > 0.5% OR dual-write mismatch > 0.1% OR dispatcher error rate rises by 2x, rollback canary
Gradual scaling of adapter worker pools and buffer sizes as we observe real traffic patterns
